_meta.source: CSSOM :hover / :focus-visible / :active / :disabled rules matched against live elements (listing detail + search results), 2026-09-10
_meta.confidence: computed rules, exact. Values are Airbnb DLS custom properties; resolved values are in tokens.json where captured.
_meta.observation: Every state is expressed through a small set of named properties (--dls-button_background_hover etc.). The state grammar is uniform across button kinds; only the property values differ per kind.

active: transform: scaleX((w-2)/w) scaleY((h-2)/h)  — the button shrinks by exactly 2px on press, not by a percentage
a ripple element: transform: scale(5); opacity: 0; transition: transform 2s, opacity 2s
focus_visible: box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px var(--palette-border-primary-inverse), 0 0 0 4px var(--palette-border-primary)  — a 2px white gap then a 2px dark ring

hover: background: var(--palette-bg-primary-hover)  — the 8px-radius grey hover pad behind the text
title: color var(--palette-grey1000) + text-decoration underline (grey1000 underline)
image / tile: transform scale(1.04) with box-shadow var(--elevation-secondary-box-shadow)
small round controls inside: transform scale(1.08)
listing_card.note: Scale on hover is reserved for imagery and round icon buttons; text never scales. Press always scales DOWN (0.92 / 0.96 / minus 2px).

hover: border-color: var(--palette-grey500)  — the #DDD border darkens to mid grey; no fill change
filter_chip.selected: not captured (no chip was selected on the page); needs a click-through

cross_cutting_rules: Focus is always a double ring: 2px gap colour + 2px ring colour, via box-shadow, never outline.
Hover on a text control is colour + underline + a soft grey pad; hover on a filled control is a darker fill; hover on imagery is scale 1.04 + elevation.
Press is a uniform shrink: minus 2px for rectangular controls, 0.92–0.96 for round/text ones.
Motion: one named easing (--motion-standard-curve-animation-timing-function), 0.2s for state changes; the press ripple is the only long transition (2s) and it is opacity-only.
Disabled never dims with opacity; it swaps to named disabled colours and removes transforms and gradients.
